classification.scope: All parallel products of affine forms, modulo free affine output terms. Not arbitrary sequential AND circuits or AES.

target_basis_audit.scope: Specific GF16 multiplication target with arbitrary mixed affine input factors and fixed RM(1,3) decoder. Uses actual field scaling on first operand, then decoder coordinate automorphism. Does not authorize arbitrary gate sorting or arbitrary target-space input symmetry.
target_basis_audit.identity: C p = B f; input scaling gives C p_prime = D f with D first row e0; D_inverse C = C P; thus C(P p_prime)=f.
target_basis_audit.proof_note: Every nonzero output covector is normalized by a unique field scaling because field multiplication gives a regular action on the15nonzero dual vectors. The eight decoder columns are exactly all four-bit columns with first coordinate1; any invertible D whose first row is e0 permutes that set.

theory_proof_chain.argument: With GF256 = GF16[z], z^16+z=1 and nu=z^2+z, N(a+bz)=a^2+ab+nu*b^2. Squaring is GF2-linear. The input tower basis and output subfield basis are invertible linear changes, so quadratic AND complexity of the four norm coordinates equals that of GF16 multiplication.
theory_proof_chain.evidence: report.json:norm_multiplier_identities; all 256 norm inputs and 256 embedding products checked.

theory_proof_chain.step: Decoder minimum distance and seven-gate exclusion
theory_proof_chain.argument: All 15 nonzero output polar matrices have rank 8. A product of two affine forms has polar rank at most 2, so every nonzero decoder word has weight at least 4. Decoder dimension is four. In a binary dimension-four code each nonzero column contributes weight eight across all 16 words. With at most seven columns, total nonzero-word weight is at most 56, but 15 words of weight at least four require at least 60. Thus at least eight products are necessary in the parallel quadratic model. An eight-product solution cannot contain an affine or linearly redundant product, since it could then be shortened to seven.

Exhaustive unique-RREF enumeration finds exactly 30 dimension-four length-eight codes of minimum distance at least four. They are exactly the coordinate-permutation orbit of C rows (255,170,204,240). Thus after gate permutation any solution has C*p = B*f modulo affine terms with B invertible.
theory_proof_chain.evidence: report.json:code_classification; 200787 subspaces and 40320 coordinate permutations checked.

theory_proof_chain.step: Output basis can be identity for this target
theory_proof_chain.argument: Substituting x by alpha*x sends the multiplication output vector f to M(alpha)*f. For any nonzero first row beta of B, there is a unique nonzero alpha with beta*M(alpha)=e0, since field scalings act regularly on nonzero dual vectors. Therefore D=B*M(alpha) has first row e0. The eight columns of C are exactly the four-bit vectors with first coordinate one. D inverse permutes this set, so D inverse*C=C*P for a coordinate permutation P. From C*p'=D*f obtain C*P*p'=f. This uses parallel-gate permutation and target-specific field input symmetry, not an arbitrary output-basis assumption.
theory_proof_chain.evidence: target-basis-report.json; all 20160 invertible B verified, using 15 scalings and 1344 decoder automorphisms.

theory_proof_chain.step: First factor can be raw bit zero while retaining identity target basis
theory_proof_chain.argument: A determinant-one field matrix sends (x,y) to (a*x+b*y,c*x+d*y). Their product differs from x*y by a*c*x^2+b*d*y^2, which is GF2-linear. Hence every individual output polar is unchanged. SL2(F16) acts transitively on the 255 nonzero binary linear forms, represented as trace(u*x+v*y), so gate zero's first nonzero factor can be raw bit zero. Adding that factor to the other factor clears its bit zero and changes only an affine term. Thus this normalization preserves both B=I and the fixed C decoder modulo affine terms.
theory_proof_chain.evidence: symmetry-report.json:SL2_normalization; all 4080 group matrices, 255 covectors, 65280 truth rows and 64770 independent operand pairs checked.

theory_proof_chain.argument: The six GL2(F2) bases of a nondegenerate operand plane yield products differing only by a linear form because h squared equals h for Boolean signals. Constants also alter a product only by an affine function. Each plane has a unique basis whose left highest set bit is below the right highest set bit and whose right coefficient at the left pivot is zero. Canonicalizing each gate therefore preserves all 28 quadratic coefficient equations. No arbitrary global gate ordering is justified after fixing C.

Independent primal swap, field scales, shear and Frobenius transformations preserve the four-dimensional target quadratic space modulo affine terms. Their pullback action partitions all 10795 binary two-planes into three orbits of sizes 510, 85 and 10200, represented by factors (1,2), (1,12), (1,16). Input substitution and free affine output correction carry any sequential circuit between equivalent first-plane cases. Affine changes of an earlier gate can be propagated through later unrestricted linear operand masks. This reduction therefore also covers unrestricted sequential circuits when their later masks and output affine decoder remain free.
theory_proof_chain.evidence: symmetry-report.json:first_plane_orbits; independent BFS exactly matches the parent's orbit receipt, and all five generator substitutions checked on 256 inputs.

normalized_probe.justification: GF16 input field scaling normalizes the all-eight-product decoder output row; RM decoder automorphisms normalize remaining invertible target basis. Determinant-one GF16 input transforms preserve all multiplication output polars and are transitive on nonzero input covectors, permitting first-left factor bit0. Affine output corrections remain free.
normalized_probe.scope: Parallel quadratic-AND GF16 multiplication only, not unrestricted dependent gates or AES.

certificate.scope: Clausal proof of the exact normalized quadratic instance; semantic completeness still depends on separately audited code/field symmetries. No dependent-gate or AES bound.

LRAT.scope: Normalized quadratic GF16 instance only. Human/finite-audited input symmetries connect it to all quadratic8-AND implementations; no arbitrary dependent-gate or AES bound.

XOR_conversion_audit.logical_contract: Signed native rows assert odd parity of signed literal truth values. Negations change the unsigned rhs by their parity; fresh gate clauses enforce each running XOR exactly, and final unit enforces that rhs. Auxiliaries are fresh and each signed row has a unique extension iff satisfied. All preexisting clauses are retained unchanged.
XOR_conversion_audit.scope: Equisatisfiability and exact bytes of native-to-plain clausal conversion only. No symmetry proof, DRAT/LRAT proof replay, sequential lower bound or AES result is implied.

sequential_search.scope: At most8 topologically ordered ANDs for GF16 multiplication with arbitrary affine combinations of previous signals and free affine output decoding. Three first-plane representative cases cover all first non-affine gates under the separately verified input symmetries. A timeout is not an exclusion. No complete AES result.
